selection_criteria: The 80 most recently published GitHub-reviewed advisories for the pip ecosystem as of 2026-08-07, capped at 2 per source repository and 1 per fixing commit, restricted to those carrying a CWE and a fixing-commit reference into their own repository whose parent is not a merge, whose fix diff is under 400 KB, and which touch reviewable Python source outside tests and docs. Ground-truth spans are the lines the fix removed, excluding spans that are entirely imports, version bumps or comments. Two fixing commits were then excluded by hand as bulk refactors whose spans mark remediation plumbing rather than the defect; the reasons are in benchmark/corpus/labelled-excluded.txt. NOT filtered by CWE: classes no 3a detector can emit are retained and reported as a stratum. Newest-first sampling makes the set post-cutoff for any model evaluated later.

pymdown-extensions: exponential-backtracking ReDoS in caret, tilde, betterem, and magiclink inline processors

findings.title: Regex with nested overlapping quantifiers enables ReDoS

evidence.why: The diff changes the host-matching regex from `[^_\W](?:[-\w]|\.(?!=$))*` to `[^_\W][-\w]*(?:\.[-\w.]+)*`, introducing an outer `*` around a group whose inner class `[-\w.]+` also matches `.` and word chars — this ambiguous nested-quantifier structure can cause catastrophic backtracking on crafted input like a long run of dots/word chars with no terminating match, and this regex runs on arbitrary user-supplied markdown text.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Removed negative lookahead widens backtracking in emphasis regex

evidence.why: STAR_EM2 changed `\*{2,}(?!\*)` to `\*{2,}`, removing the lookahead that previously disambiguated runs of asterisks; combined with the surrounding `(?:[^\*]|\*{2,})+?` alternation this creates more overlapping ways to match the same input, increasing backtracking potential on pathological asterisk sequences in user-supplied markdown.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Removed negative lookahead widens backtracking in subscript regex

evidence.why: SUB2 changed `~{2,}(?!~)` to `~{2,}`, removing disambiguation in the alternation `(?:[^\s~]|~{2,})+?`, increasing ambiguous match paths for crafted tilde runs in markdown input.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Removed negative lookahead widens backtracking in superscript regex

evidence.why: SUP2 changed `\^{2,}(?!\^)` to `\^{2,}`, removing disambiguation in the alternation `(?:[^\^\s]|\^{2,})+?`, increasing ambiguous match paths for crafted caret runs in markdown input.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: pymdown-extensions: exponential-backtracking ReDoS in caret, tilde, betterem, and magiclink inline processors

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

findings.title: Namespace prefix search uses unescaped LIKE, losing segment-boundary and wildcard escaping

evidence.why: The diff replaces _namespace_prefix_condition (which escaped % and _ and anchored on a `.` segment boundary) with a bare `store.prefix LIKE %s` built from unescaped _namespace_to_text, so a namespace value containing `%` or `_` acts as a wildcard and prefix `foo` now also matches `foobar`, causing unintended cross-namespace data exposure in search().

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix match conditions use unescaped LIKE without segment anchoring

evidence.why: The diff replaces the regex-based _namespace_match_pattern (segment-anchored, metacharacter-escaped) with `prefix LIKE %s` built from _namespace_to_text without escaping literal `%`/`_`, so user-controlled path segments containing those characters are interpreted as wildcards and prefixes no longer respect segment boundaries (e.g. `foo` matches `foobar`), leaking namespaces that should be isolated.

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

findings.title: SQLite namespace_prefix search uses unescaped LIKE instead of escaped GLOB with segment anchoring

evidence.why: The diff drops _namespace_prefix_condition (GLOB-based, escaped, segment-anchored, case-sensitive) in favor of `s.prefix LIKE ?` with an unescaped, case-insensitive pattern built from _namespace_to_text, letting a namespace label containing `%`/`_` act as a wildcard and letting differently-cased or prefix-sharing namespaces (e.g. `foo` vs `foobar`, `Foo` vs `foo`) cross-match, leaking data across intended namespace boundaries.

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix conditions use unescaped LIKE, dropping segment-boundary regex matching

evidence.why: The diff removes the segment-aware _namespace_match_pattern/NS_MATCH_FUNCTION logic and replaces prefix/suffix matching with plain `prefix LIKE ?` over unescaped _namespace_to_text output, so labels containing `%`/`_` behave as wildcards and prefixes no longer stop at segment boundaries, allowing unintended namespace matches.

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Upgrade now takes effect before request body is read, causing request smuggling

evidence.why: cb_on_headers_complete now returns 2 (skip body) immediately when upgrade is detected, instead of deferring the upgrade until the body is fully consumed as before; if the application declines the upgrade and treats the connection as HTTP/1.1, the unread body bytes are left in the stream and get parsed as the start of the next request, enabling request smuggling/desync (this reverts the fix described in the deleted CHANGES/13016.bugfix.rst).

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Payload reader skipped for upgrade requests with a body

evidence.why: the added 'and not self._upgraded' condition prevents a StreamReader payload from being created for upgrade requests that have Content-Length/chunked bodies, so callers that decline the upgrade (e.g. reject the websocket) can no longer read/drain the body, leaving unread bytes to be misinterpreted as the next request on the same connection.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Removed symlink-clamping resolution allows extraction path escape

evidence.why: The diff replaces _safe_resolve(rootfs_dir, rel_parts[:-1]) with a plain os.path.join(rootfs_dir, *rel_parts[:-1]), so a symlink planted earlier in the archive (e.g. evil -> /) is no longer clamped and a later member evil/passwd is written through it onto the host.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Deferred hardlink copy no longer re-resolves endpoints, enabling symlink escape

evidence.why: deferred_links now stores raw dest/src paths computed at defer time instead of rel_parts re-resolved via _safe_resolve at copy time, so a symlink planted by a later member can redirect the shutil.copy2 write or read outside rootfs_dir.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Hardlink source path built without symlink clamping

evidence.why: _defer_hardlink now computes link_src = os.path.join(rootfs_dir, *rel_lparts) directly instead of resolving through _safe_resolve, so a linkname routed through a planted symlink can cause shutil.copy2 to read/copy a host file into the rootfs.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Directory extraction no longer removes pre-existing symlink before makedirs

evidence.why: The removed `if os.path.islink(dest): _remove_fstree(dest)` check means a symlink planted at a directory's name is no longer replaced before os.makedirs/chmod, so operations can act through the symlink onto its target.

findings.title: Restore no longer clamps destination through _safe_dest, enabling symlink-based path escape

evidence.why: The diff removes the `dest = _safe_dest(container_name, dest); if dest is None: continue` block, so a crafted backup archive containing a symlink like rootfs/evil -> / followed by rootfs/evil/passwd is written through the symlink onto the host filesystem.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Hardlink source no longer clamped inside container during restore

evidence.why: link_src is now taken directly from _dest_path(member.linkname) without the removed _safe_dest(..., follow_final=True) clamp, so a linkname routed through a planted symlink can cause a host file to be copied into the restored rootfs.

findings.title: Materialised file writes no longer clamp parent path through symlinks

AWS Bedrock AgentCore: Improper neutralization of argument delimiters in the Python SDK install_packages()

findings.title: Regex now allows arbitrary characters in pip extras group, enabling shell injection

evidence.why: The extras group pattern changed from a restricted charset ([a-zA-Z0-9._,\-]*) to (\[.*\]), permitting any characters including $(), backticks, spaces, and semicolons inside brackets, e.g. 'pkg[$(whoami)]' now passes validation.

remediation.summary: Pass an argument list instead of a shell string, or quote with shlex.quote().

findings.title: Removed shlex.quote before building shell command string

evidence.why: packages_str is now built via plain ' '.join(packages) without shell-quoting, so any package string that reaches this point (including one that slips past the weakened regex) is inserted unquoted into the `pip install ...` shell command.

remediation.summary: Pass an argument list instead of a shell string, or quote with shlex.quote().
